roundShape: full round, as the architect set it: the disk watcher and the runner-job wait are in cluster.sh's run path. Driving pod uid d0493a3a-de74-409a-a3ce-671f96d3d7a8 (the pod was replaced mid-round; the first attempt's evidence died with the one before it, uid ca16bc21, and every measurement below was taken again on this one). Nothing else of mine ran on the pod during the live checks, and no suite ran while the copy was up.

implementerProof.how: The watcher's new behaviour was driven on the real copy rather than read (run lt-20261031t211910-c81b): a kubectl wrapper made the Postgres df report 1% free, so the watcher wanted to act, and failed every read of the lock ConfigMap for one poll. At 21:38:11Z the watcher logged `step pollfail: the disk watcher records nothing and stops no job at this poll; it reads the lock again at the next one`, with the guard's own note carrying kubectl's words (`could not read the lock … after 3 tries (the last one said: error: the connection to the server was refused (fake) …)`); with the lock readable again at the next poll it recorded the failure, `step pollfail failed: pg_disk of postgres: … 1.0 GiB free (1% of it), under the 15% …`, and stopped the load. `the disk watcher stops, recording nothing and stopping no job` - the line for a lock that names another run - appears zero times, so nothing was stopped wrongly. The clean 1x step of the same run refused nothing: no `could not read the lock` and no `no longer names run` line, config.dashboard sse, 1,438 live frames, 0 order violations, 3.99 events/s committed, 10,752 of 10,752 requests 2xx, no step-failed.json, and summary.json carries no live.transport field at all, which is the omitempty change. The log is dispatch://INFRA-598/artifact/round11-watcher-live-txt, uploaded while the copy was still up.

failures.criterion: The architect's item 2: cluster.test.sh green over repeated runs under CPU load
failures.evidence: It is not, and the failing assertion is one of this round's own: under four busy loops on this 3-CPU pod the suite went red on one of three runs, iter-2, with `FAIL: collect --run lt-20261031t230329-309e read the lock, which names another run, although it reaches no pod of the copy` (iter-1 and iter-3: 54 PASS, 0 FAIL). The same assertion failed on the only complete run of my first attempt, on the pod that was replaced, so it is two reds in four loaded runs. The mechanism is in the file and needs no load to be read: cluster.test.sh:2833 takes `collect_calls=$(wc -l <"$fake/kubectl.log")` and :2841 asserts that no LINE after that position in the shared kubectl.log mentions `configmap dispatch-loadtest-lock`. The fixture's own heartbeat daemon patches the lock on its own cycle and writes that line into the same file, and the fake sleep makes its cycles fast, so a patch that lands while collect runs is read as collect reading the lock. This is the class I failed round 9 on, and this round's own fix is the cure that was not applied here: the session-tagged kubectl-calls.log, which pairs calls by the caller's session, is used by guarded_by_lock_read but not by this assertion. Remedy for the implementer: assert over kubectl-calls.log restricted to collect's own session (no line of that session names the lock), or stop the fixture's daemons around the assertion. Nothing of the product is implicated: collect's own behaviour under another run's lock I drove live in round 8 and it was right then and is right here.

proof.criterion: Review round 7: an unreadable lock makes the disk watcher record nothing at that poll and read it again at the next, and the guard's note carries kubectl's own words
proof.surface: GKE namespace loadtest, from this Legion worker pod
proof.command: cluster.sh up … && seed && step 1x 1 --duration 3m, then step pollfail 1 --duration 5m under a kubectl wrapper whose df reports 1% free (FLAG_LOW) and whose lock read fails while FLAG_LOCK exists; the lock flag was set at 21:37:41Z and cleared when the note appeared at 21:38:11Z; then down
proof.observed: One `the disk watcher records nothing and stops no job at this poll; it reads the lock again at the next one`, the guard's note carrying kubectl's own refusal, then at the next poll `step pollfail failed: pg_disk of postgres: … 1.0 GiB free (1% of it)` with the load stopped and step-failed.json holding kind pg_disk; zero occurrences of the stop-for-another-run line. The 1x step of the same copy was clean: no guard note at all, sse transport, 1,438 frames, 0 order violations, 10,752/10,752 2xx, no step-failed.json, and no live.transport in summary.json
proof.negativeControl: The clean 1x step is one half of the control and the injected step the other: the same copy, the same command, and the only difference is the wrapper; and the suite against 183c0d7f's cluster.sh fails after 51 PASS with `runner_stop's note does not carry what the failed read of the lock said`, the red state of one of this round's new cases

notes: I ran the leftover check the rule asks for after stopping the named job loop11-infra-598 by proc://loop11-infra-598/kill: `ps -eo pid,args | grep -v grep | grep -E 'memory.usage_in_bytes|sleep 2|loop11.sh|cluster.test.sh'` printed nothing, so this time the kill left nothing behind.
